Mia C: Nightly eval (job 2026-03-18-23) flagged a reproducible quality regression on the int8 quantized build. Failures concentrated on instruction-heavy prompts with long prefixes. Baseline float16 is fine. Strangely, when I run the same eval with prefix cache disabled the regression disappears. Anyone seen cache-related nondeterminism after quantization?

Leo H: Hmm, cache-related nondet rings a bell. Can you paste a minimal failing prompt id + the env/batch settings used in the nightly job?

Mia C: Prompt ids 1254 and 1289 are the clearest. Example (redacted): 'Given these constraints, write step-by-step plumbing instructions...' Baseline -> correct troubleshooting steps. Quant int8 -> short, tangential steps and invented parts. Nightly job: dedicated-repl-5, model: rdx-3b-int8, batch_size=32, continuous-batching=on, prefix_cache=on.

Samir: Try a replay with prefix cache off and batch_size=1 to isolate ordering. Also run with seed fixed. Quick command I use:
```
redwood-eval replay --job 2026-03-18-23 --no-prefix-cache --batch-size 1 --seed 42
```

EvalBot: [nightly-eval] job 2026-03-18-23 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/2026-03-18-23/ (contains failures.json, logs.tar.gz)

Mia C: I ran Samir's replay. With --no-prefix-cache + batch=1 outputs match float16 baseline. With cache on and batch>1 divergence is intermittent but reproducible across runs (same prompts sometimes fail, sometimes pass).

Leo H: Intermittent + batch-dependent + cache implicated => likely a collision or eviction ordering effect. Two guesses: 1) shorthash collisions in prefix->slot mapping are higher for quantized model (maybe different tokenization/kv fingerprint). 2) batch interleaving changes the order KV entries get written and evicted.

Kaitlyn: Also consider that quantization can alter internal key/values layout (different rounding/padding) which might change the effective key bytes used for hash. If our cache uses a low-bit shorthash (e.g., 32-bit) collisions could spike. Do we have collision metrics?

Samir: Pulled the replay traces and computed shorthash collision rates across the eval set. Quick numbers: baseline float16 collision_rate=0.02%, rdx-3b-int8 collision_rate=0.78% (same batch shape). Eviction churn also ~3x higher on int8 under bursty loads.

Mia C: Those numbers line up with what I see. Turning off prefix cache in canary removes regression.

Leo H: Short-term mitigation: disable prefix cache for the int8 rollout or force smaller batch sizes. Medium-term: bump shorthash to 64-bit OR include tenant+model+seqlen salt into hash. Also we should add a per-request slot nonce to avoid aliasing across concurrent batches.

Kaitlyn: Agree. I'll draft an RFC covering: 1) safety toggle for cache per-model/variant, 2) hash upgrade plan, 3) test matrix (quantization x batch x seqlen). Also will schedule a bench to reproduce at scale.

Samir: I'll implement a deterministic reproducer (unit+integration) that fuzzes tokenization offsets, seq len padding, and quantized weight permutations to provoke collisions. Plan to add regression test that runs in CI nightly.

Mia C: For immediate action I recommend pausing the int8 canary until we ship a hotfix or at least disable prefix cache for that model. @Kaitlyn can you coordinate with product/infra to flip the flag?

Kaitlyn: Yes, I'll file a config change (toggle: models.rdx-3b-int8.prefix_cache=false) and notify infra. Will also create an incident flag so PMs know. :thumbsup:

Leo H: Logging follow-ups: add per-request cache keys to debug logs (masked) and emit collision counters to metrics. That will let us triage future regressions faster.

Samir: On it. I'll open PRs: 1) add collision metric, 2) reproducible test harness, 3) quick hash bump prototype.

Mia C: Thanks everyone. Saved the failing examples to the eval artifacts and linked them in the ticket. If anyone wants to look I put quick diffs in s3://redwood-evals/triage/1832001234/diffs.json. :eyes:
